transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-02
Start: 14:30 PDT
Duration: ~64 minutes
Attendees: Aaron Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Lin (Redwood SE), Janelle Ortiz (Clearwave - Head of ML Ops), Ravi Menon (Clearwave - Platform Eng), Sophie Clarke (Clearwave - PM)

Summary: (auto-gen, may be incomplete)
- Align on go/no-go thresholds for the POC: latency p95, throughput, model quality (F1/accuracy), and cost-per-million-tokens target.
- Agree on reporting artifact: CSV + benchmark dashboard + short exec summary.
- 3-week pilot timeline: integration week, benchmark week, analysis & signoff week.

Topics covered:
- Benchmark harness and what constitutes production-like traffic
- Data sanitization and VPC access
- Acceptance thresholds and pass/fail rules
- Report format and cadence

Action items (in-call recap): Aaron to send harness; Ravi to set up VPC; Maya to propose canary thresholds; Sophie to finalize business success criteria.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Aaron (AE): Hey everybody, thanks for joining. Can you hear me okay?
[00:03] Janelle: Yeah we can hear you, thanks. Sorry running a little late, whole morning was calendar land.
[00:06] Aaron: No worries. Quick intros? We'll go around and then jump into the acceptance checklist.
[00:12] Sophie: Sophie Clarke, PM on the personalization team, I'll be owning the success metrics from product side.
[00:16] Ravi: Ravi Menon, platform engineering. I'll do infra and VPC stuff.
[00:19] Janelle: Janelle Ortiz, Head of ML Ops, I'll be the final sign-off.
[00:23] Maya (SE): Maya Lin, Redwood SE, I'll run the benchmark harness with you and help tune batching/quantization.
[00:27] Aaron: Great. We put together a draft acceptance spec — want to walk through thresholds and make sure this maps to your business goals.
[00:33] Janelle: Sounds good. The two big things for us are latency for interactive flows and costs for high volume nightly jobs.
[00:38] Sophie: Right—if latency is too high our UX team will push back, and if cost per million tokens spikes we can't justify the migration.

[01:05] Aaron: So for interactive calls we proposed p95 latency under 200 ms for the Redwood-hosted model variant with our recommended batching. For batch jobs, we want throughput of at least 1k tokens per second per GPU and unit cost below $12 per 1M generated tokens during the pilot. Those are soft starts, we can adjust.
[01:22] Ravi: Sorry can you re-state the cost number? Was that $12 or $1.2?
[01:24] Aaron: $12 per one million generated tokens, yeah. That's our target for the quantized model profile we recommended.
[01:28] Janelle: That number seems reasonable as a starting point, but we need guardrails. What happens if latency meets threshold but cost is 20% higher?
[01:33] Maya: In the runbook we have a fallback policy: if cost is >15% above target and forecasted spend for the pilot exceeds budget, we trigger a quiesce to a cheaper model variant and flag for manual review. That's one of the go/no-go gates.

[02:10] Sophie: Can we get that spelled out as a pass/fail matrix? Product wants an explicit go/no-go so execs can decide quickly.
[02:14] Aaron: Absolutely. Draft matrix idea: PASS if all mandatory gates green. Mandatory gates: p95 latency < 200 ms; batch throughput >= 1k tokens/s per GPU; quality: intent classification F1 >= 0.87 on the agreed eval set; cost per 1M tokens <= $12. If any mandatory gate fails, it's a NO-GO. Optional gates could be availability > 99.5% and end-to-end median latency < 90ms.
[02:33] Janelle: I like the F1 number but we need clarity on the eval set. Is it synthetic or production-sampled?
[02:37] Maya: We recommend two eval tracks: 1) production-sampled holdout — customer-provided, sanitized; and 2) synthetic adversarial set Redwood will provide — to stress parts of the model. For sign-off we'll prioritize the production-sampled metrics.
[02:46] Ravi: On the infra side we need a clear list of ports and roles for the VPC, and we need the IAM policy in advance so we can whitelist.
[02:50] Aaron: We'll attach a minimal VPC integration checklist in the repo.

[03:12] Janelle: Timeline-wise we were hoping for a 3-week pilot. Is that still the plan?
[03:15] Aaron: Yes. Week 1: integration and sample data exchange; Week 2: run benchmarks (throughput/latency/quality); Week 3: analysis, remediation, and final sign-off. We also recommended a two-day buffer for unexpected infra hiccups.
[03:24] Sophie: For reporting — product wants a single CSV with per-query latency, model variant tag, token counts, and pass/fail flags plus an executive one-pager.
[03:30] Maya: Redwood will produce the CSV and we'll push a lightweight dashboard link to Grafana metrics; the CSV feeds the exec summary template. We'll include token-level cost calculations and per-route breakdowns.

[04:05] Ravi: About sample traffic — we can produce a 48-hour slice of anonymized traffic for day-0 testing. Will that be enough?
[04:09] Aaron: For the initial integration yes. For throughput validation we'll need a replay mode that simulates the production qps distribution — we'll run that in week 2.
[04:14] Ravi: Ok. For replay can you confirm whether the KV cache behavior will be simulated? We've had surprises when caches warm up in production.
[04:18] Maya: Good point — our harness has a KV cache warmup step where we replay prefixes to replicate real cache hit ratios. It'll be in the runbook.

[05:00] Sophie: On quality metrics, besides F1 for intent, we need a semantic similarity threshold for embeddings used by search — target cosine > 0.92 on our benchmark pairs.
[05:05] Aaron: Noted. We'll include embedding recall/precision checks.

[05:40] Janelle: Are you planning to run quantized weights in the pilot? We have concerns about hallucination drift.
[05:44] Maya: We'll test 4-bit quantization (LLM.int4 style) as an optional variant. Quality gates apply equally — if intent F1 drops > 3% relative to fp16 baseline, that variant fails the gate. We'll document exact measurement method.

[06:20] Ravi: Logging and audit — we need request-level audit logs and token-level cost breakdown for our finance team. Retention is 90 days for the pilot. Does Redwood support that in private deployment?
[06:25] Aaron: Yes, logs can be exported to your S3 and we can enable token-level billing detail. For hosted we'll provide the same exports with redaction options.

[07:00] Sophie: Can we see an example of the reporting template?
[07:02] Aaron: I'll send the template as part of the benchmark harness repo. It has CSV schema, a sample dashboard link, and an executive one-pager example.

[07:46] Janelle: Ok, let's walk through the proposed pass/fail matrix live and make sure the language is unambiguous for legal and finance.
[07:51] Aaron: Sure. I'll read it and you tell me if it maps: Mandatory gates - all must be met: 1) p95 latency < 200 ms for interactive flows measured at the same concurrency as production; 2) Batch throughput >= 1k tokens/s per GPU using the recommended batch/kv profile; 3) Intent classification F1 >= 0.87 on production-sampled holdout; 4) Unit cost <= $12 per 1M generated tokens during the benchmark window. Do you want me to repeat anything?
[08:14] Sophie: I'd add 'measured over a 30-minute stable window' for latency to avoid fluke spikes causing failure.
[08:18] Aaron: Good call. We'll make the latency gate 'p95 latency < 200 ms measured over a continuous 30-minute stable window during benchmarking'.
[08:22] Janelle: And for cost, is that aggregated for the whole pilot or per-hour?
[08:25] Maya: Aggregated projected cost normalized to per 1M tokens for the pilot run. The reporting will show both instantaneous cost and extrapolated pilot spend.
[08:31] Ravi: For availability optional gate, we can do 99.5% during the test window but production SLA will be a separate negotiation.

[09:06] Sophie: What about tie-breaker rules? If F1 is 0.866 (below 0.87) but latency and cost are well under targets, do we auto-fail?
[09:12] Aaron: Our proposed stance: mandatory gates are strict unless there's a documented business tolerance exception signed off by the stakeholders ahead of time. So yes, 0.866 would be a NO-GO unless the customer gives a waiver. But we can set a soft-warning threshold (e.g., 0.85–0.87) for remediation steps.
[09:29] Janelle: That seems fair. We'll draft a waiver process if needed.

[10:00] Ravi: For the runbook, can you list the exact experiments you'll run? Things like batching curves, KV cache warmup, quant profiles?
[10:04] Maya: Yes: 1) baseline latency/throughput with recommended batch sizes; 2) batch size sweep to find cost/latency Pareto; 3) quantization variants (fp16, int8, int4) with quality comparison; 4) cache warmup and cold-start runs; 5) replay with production qps distribution. Each experiment will produce a CSV and aggregated metrics.

[11:02] Sophie: For the exec one-pager, finance will want delta vs current infra spend. Can Redwood help estimate delta cost relative to Clearwave's current GPU infra?
[11:07] Aaron: We can provide an approximate delta calculation if you share current utilization and pricing assumptions. It'll be part of the extrapolated pilot spend section.

[12:00] Janelle: Any security constraints? We use customer-managed KMS and require SOC2 evidence.
[12:04] Aaron: Redwood supports KMS integration and we can share SOC 2 Type II attestation and encryption-in-transit docs. We'll attach those to the repo as security exhibits.

[13:20] Ravi: Small ask: can you include per-route traces so we can understand tail latency causes?
[13:24] Maya: Yes, we'll include per-route traces and token-level breakdowns, and link to the tracing dashboard with flame graphs.

[14:00] Sophie: Ok, let's lock the dates. Aaron said he'd send the harness by Tuesday 5/5. Can we agree to start integration on 5/10?
[14:05] Aaron: 5/10 works for Redwood. We'll plan a 30-minute kickoff then.
[14:08] Janelle: Perfect. And final sign-off cadence — we'll aim to have a decision meeting on 5/29? That's three weeks after kickoff with buffer.
[14:12] Aaron: Yes, 5/29 works as decision meeting. We'll plan a short pre-read one day before with the executive summary.

[15:00] Sophie: One last thing — reporting format must include a canonical run id and timestamp so finance can reconcile cost numbers to the bills.
[15:05] Maya: Run id will be included in CSV header and in all dashboard exports.

[15:40] Janelle: Thanks all. Are there any outstanding blockers we missed?
[15:43] Ravi: IAM policy sample from Redwood would unblock me; otherwise infra is straightforward.
[15:47] Aaron: We'll attach a minimal IAM template with the repo.

[16:10] Aaron: Quick recap of next steps: I'll send the harness, IAM template, runbook, and reporting template by 5/5. Maya will propose canary config by 5/9. Ravi will provision VPC by 5/8. Sophie will finalize success criteria doc and sign-off by 5/11. Meet again for kickoff 5/10 and decision meeting 5/29.
[16:30] Janelle: That matches our expectations. Thanks everyone.
[16:33] Aaron: Thanks, we'll follow up in email with links.
[16:36] (call ends)

Notes:
- The transcript contains some ASR artifacts and occasional speaker mislabels; treat names and acronyms as approximations.
- Files referenced during the call: benchmark_harness repo (link to be provided), acceptance_template.csv (example), SOC2-exhibit.pdf (security docs).

End of transcript.
